title: Volume of Cylinders
seo_title: Grade 7 Volume of Cylinders Worksheets with Answers (MATATAG Math 7)
standard_text: Explain inductively the volume of a cylinder using the area of a circle, leading to the identification of the formula; find the volume of a cylinder; solve problems involving the volumes of cylinders.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 volume of cylinders worksheets for the DepEd MATATAG curriculum: V = πr²h, radius and diameter, missing dimensions and real-life problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Halve the diameter to get the radius.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A cylinder is like a stack of equal circles. Its volume is base area × height.
  • The base is a circle with area πr², so V = πr²h.
  • If you know the diameter, halve it to get the radius first.
  • Volume is in cubic units: cm³ or m³. 1,000 cm³ = 1 L.

Examples

Example

r = 5 cm, h = 10 cm

π × 5² × 10 = 250π

Answer: ≈ 785 cm³

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Diameter as radiusHalve the diameter first.
Not squaringr² means r × r.
Using 2πr2πr is the circumference, not the base area.

items.q: A cylinder has a radius of 3 cm. What is the area of its circular base? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: Area = π × r × r = 3.14 × 3 × 3 = 3.14 × 9 = 28.26 square centimeters. 18.84 is 3.14 × 6 (r × 2, not r × r). 113.04 uses 6 cm, the diameter.

items.q: A can has a diameter of 10 cm. What is the area of its circular base? (Use π ≈ 3.14.)
items.e: r is half the diameter: 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm. Area = 3.14 × 5 × 5 = 3.14 × 25 = 78.5 square centimeters. 314 uses the diameter as r, and 31.4 is the circumference.
